definitions.gloss: matchmaking; acting as go-between for a marriage
definitions.explanation: The act of introducing a prospective bride and groom and facilitating their marriage, or presiding over the wedding ceremony as a formal witness.

examples.japanese: ⟦{上司|じょうし}→上司：03286_joushi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{媒酌|ばいしゃく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{頼|たの}んだ→頼む：01104_tanomu⟧。
examples.english: I asked my boss to serve as matchmaker.

examples.japanese: ⟦{媒酌人|ばいしゃくにん}→媒酌人：26257_baishakunin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{両家|りょうけ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{引|ひ}き{合|あ}わせた。
examples.english: The matchmaker introduced the two families to each other.

examples.japanese: ⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{媒酌人|ばいしゃくにん}→媒酌人：26257_baishakunin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{立|た}てない→立てる：01196_tateru⟧⟦{結婚式|けっこんしき}→結婚式：05493_kekkonshiki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}えている→増える：01183_fueru⟧。
examples.english: Recently, weddings without a formal matchmaker have been increasing.

notes:
A formal term from traditional Japanese marriage customs. The ⟦{媒酌人|ばいしゃくにん}→媒酌人：26257_baishakunin⟧ (matchmaker/go-between) was historically a respected married couple who introduced the bride and groom, helped negotiate between families, and presided over the wedding ceremony. While ⟦{見合|みあ}い→見合い：14159_miai⟧ (arranged marriage meetings) still occur, the formal role of ⟦{媒酌人|ばいしゃくにん}→媒酌人：26257_baishakunin⟧ has become much less common in modern Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{媒酌人|ばいしゃくにん}→媒酌人：26257_baishakunin⟧: matchmaker; go-between
- {媒酌|ばいしゃく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{務|つと}める→務める：10446_tsutomeru⟧: to serve as matchmaker
- {媒酌|ばいしゃく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{頼|たの}む→頼む：01104_tanomu⟧: to ask someone to be matchmaker
- ⟦{媒酌人|ばいしゃくにん}→媒酌人：26257_baishakunin⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{立|た}てる→立てる：01196_tateru⟧: to have a formal matchmaker

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{仲人|なこうど}→仲人：16691_nakoudo⟧: matchmaker; go-between — more commonly used in everyday language; largely interchangeable
- ⟦{見合|みあ}い→見合い：14159_miai⟧: arranged meeting for marriage — the meeting itself, not the matchmaking role
- ⟦お{見合|みあ}い→お見合い：05642_omiai⟧: arranged marriage meeting (polite form)
